blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Most modern supply chains are global. A single product — your phone, your coffee, your shoes — may visit five or six countries before it reaches you. Each country adds something: raw materials, components, labour, packaging or transport.

Global chains are cheaper and more flexible. But they also bring extra challenges. Currencies move. Borders slow things down. A political change can close a route overnight.

Globalisation has made supply chains longer — and the world a little smaller.

items.q: According to the text, how many countries may one product visit?
items.why: "may visit five or six countries before it reaches you."

items.q: What does each country add to the product?
items.why: "Each country adds something: raw materials, components, labour, packaging or transport."

items.q: According to the text, global chains are…
items.why: "Global chains are cheaper and more flexible."

items.q: The text says a political change can "close a route overnight." This suggests that…
options: global chains can face sudden problems
items.why: Inferência: se uma rota pode fechar de repente, a cadeia global corre riscos inesperados.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Global supply chains have no problems.
One product can cross many borders.
items.why: Inferência: o texto fala em moedas, fronteiras e rotas que fecham — logo, há problemas.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James mostrando a viagem de uma barra de chocolate a um novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Come here, let me show you something. This is just one chocolate bar. But look at the map — this small bar visits five countries before it reaches the shop.

It starts in Brazil. That's where the cocoa grows, on a farm. The farmer picks the beans and they travel by ship to Europe. So that is country number two.

In the Netherlands, a factory turns the beans into chocolate. Then the chocolate goes to Germany. In Germany they add sugar and milk, and they make the bar. That is countries three and four.

After that, the bar goes to a packaging plant in Poland. They put it in the box you see in the shop. Five countries, and the bar is not even in your hand yet!

So you can see why this job is not simple. Every border means paperwork. Currencies move up and down. And if one route closes, the whole plan changes. That is why we need good partners in every country.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many countries does the chocolate bar visit?
items.why: "this small bar visits five countries before it reaches the shop."

items.q: Where does the cocoa grow?
items.why: "It starts in Brazil. That's where the cocoa grows, on a farm."

items.q: What happens in Poland?
items.why: "the bar goes to a packaging plant in Poland. They put it in the box."

items.q: Why does James say the job is "not simple"?
options: Because of borders, currencies and routes
Because the bar is very small
Because he does not like maps
items.why: Inferência: ele lista fronteiras, moedas e rotas que podem fechar — por isso é complexo.

items.q: Why does James say they need good partners in every country?
options: Because he has too many friends
To handle the many steps and risks
items.why: Inferência: com muitos países e riscos, bons parceiros ajudam a manter a cadeia funcionando.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our company is global: we work in many countries." Global means…
items.why: Global = global, do mundo todo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The phone factory buys each ___ from a different country."
items.why: Component = componente, uma peça do produto.

items.q: "We pay for the labour of the workers." Labour means…
items.why: Labour = mão de obra, o trabalho das pessoas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We pay in dollars, but their ___ is the euro."
items.why: Currency = moeda de um país.

items.q: "At the border, the truck must show its papers." A border is…
items.why: Border = fronteira, a linha entre dois países.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We will roll out the new route next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar, começar aos poucos.

items.q: "The manager must sign off on the shipping plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente.

items.q: "The team pushed back on the new price." They…
options: did not like it and said so
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We ran into a problem at the border." To run into a problem means to…
items.why: Run into = topar com, encontrar de repente.

items.q: "The two offices need to keep in touch every day." To keep in touch means to…
items.why: Keep in touch = manter contato.
